 1.1 Fix $0<\rho\le1$, an input law $P$, and an $M$-word codebook drawn independently from $P^n$. Use maximum-likelihood decoding with the lowest-index tie rule. If message $m$ is sent and $y^n$ is received with $W^n(y^n\mid x_m^n)>0$, an error implies some competitor has likelihood at least the true likelihood. Hence its error indicator is at most $\left(\sum_{j\ne m}\left[\frac{W^n(y^n\mid x_j^n)}{W^n(y^n\mid x_m^n)}\right]^{1/(1+\rho)}\right)^\rho,$ which is at least one on every error event; outputs of zero true likelihood carry no channel mass. [F1, given, algebra]
 
-1.2 For fixed $P$, write $A_y(\rho)=\sum_xP(x)W(y\mid x)^{1/(1+\rho)}$ and $S(\rho)=\sum_yA_y(\rho)^{1+\rho}$. If $W(y\mid x)>0$, [F8] and the chain rule give $\left.\frac{d}{d\rho}W(y\mid x)^{1/(1+\rho)}\right|_{\rho=0}=-W(y\mid x)\ln W(y\mid x)$; if $W(y\mid x)=0$, that term is identically zero. Thus, for $q_y=A_y(0)=(PW)(y)>0$, $$A_y'(0)=-\sum_{x:W(y\mid x)>0}P(x)W(y\mid x)\ln W(y\mid x).$$ On a neighborhood of $0$ where $A_y(\rho)>0$, write $A_y(\rho)^{1+\rho}=\exp((1+\rho)\ln A_y(\rho))$. By [F7]–[F8] and the product and chain rules, its derivative at zero is $q_y\ln q_y+A_y'(0)$. If $q_y=0$, every $P(x)W(y\mid x)=0$, so $A_y(\rho)=0$ for all $\rho\ge0$ and its outer term vanishes identically. Summing the finite terms gives $$S'(0)=\sum_{y:q_y>0}q_y\ln q_y-\sum_{x,y:P(x)W(y\mid x)>0}P(x)W(y\mid x)\ln W(y\mid x)=-I(P,W),$$ because [F5] expands $I(P,W)=\sum_{x,y:PW>0}P(x)W(y\mid x)\ln\frac{W(y\mid x)}{q_y}$. Since $S(0)=1$ and $E_0(\rho,P)=-\ln S(\rho)$, the right derivative is $\partial_\rho E_0(0,P)=I(P,W)$. [F2, F5, F7, F8, given]
+1.2 For fixed $P$, write $A_y(\rho)=\sum_xP(x)W(y\mid x)^{1/(1+\rho)}$ and $S(\rho)=\sum_yA_y(\rho)^{1+\rho}$. By [F7]–[F8] and the product and chain rules, its derivative at zero is $q_y\ln q_y+A_y'(0)$. If $q_y=0$, every $P(x)W(y\mid x)=0$, so $A_y(\rho)=0$ for all $\rho\ge0$ and its outer term vanishes identically.
